newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 8 to 807 in latest week. [CORRECTED 20:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 8 to 807 in latest week. [CORRECTED 20:40 GMT]

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 807 as of Jan. 31, down eight from the prior week and 114 above (corrects from below) the year-ago total of 693, Baker Hughes Inc. said Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by five to 680, while rigs working offshore remained 107. The number of rigs active in inland waters fell three to 20.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Louisiana, which was down nine, Oklahoma, which was down four and Pennsylvania, which was up three.
The Gulf of Mexico had 102 rigs.

A total of 333 rigs were exploring for crude oil, unchanged from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas was down nine at 472, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects rose by one to two.
In Canada, the number of working rigs was down one at 414 versus 366 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 163 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Jan. 31, up one from a week ago.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 183, was 89.1 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area remained unchanged at 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 99.1 pct.
The worldwide rig count rose six to 563 out of a total fleet of 606, making the utilization rate 92.9 percent.
